mathematical_checks.area: Section 3 deterministic comparison and cell modulus
mathematical_checks.details: The three deterministic replacements give O(log n); the subgradient replacement follows from the retained cell lemma and local Laplacian growth. The interval martingale estimate then gives the frozen local-time approximation. The pointwise identity and cell modulus remain available independently of the probability event, as required by the exit-time and squared-Green arguments.

mathematical_checks.area: Coarse exit bootstrap and downstream contact input
mathematical_checks.details: Stopping at exit or the first Green-martingale threshold gives a deterministic bound on the stopping time without first assuming exit finiteness. Local-time and bracket bounds hold through the stopped time, so Freedman excludes the threshold event. The subsequently used exit comparison and deterministic geometry retain their hypotheses.

The Dynkin identity has the correct signs. The bracket of the squared-Green martingale is bounded by the same weighted energy, allowing self-normalized Freedman followed by Young absorption. The planar shift yields a first-departure sum of order r_n, while higher dimensions give O(log n). The resulting bounds extend from lattice sites to cells and then to all space, supplying the all-dimensional one-sided estimate used later.

Dropping the nonpositive endpoint contribution and the nonnegative excess moment gives (b-r_n)_+ <= C(r_n^((3-d)/2) sqrt(log n)+1), independently of the excess-volume estimate. This is a valid stronger byproduct and does not change a frozen statement.

Outside the inner ball its potential vanishes. The all-dimensional estimate ell_tilde <= 2 min(U_E^+,sup|U_E|)+C r_n q_n is valid and provides L <= C r_n q_n^(1/d), which is the input required by the imported shared outer-radius proof.

mathematical_checks.area: Shared cap estimate and near/far reduction in Section 7
mathematical_checks.details: The probe lies outside D_n; the cap contributes negatively by at least c t^(1-d) per unit volume, and dropping other negative contributions is correctly written as an inequality. The cap bound and the weighted potential F imply both hypotheses of the frozen near/far lemma with C lambda. Crossing and Young absorption then give w <= C lambda (log n)^d in every dimension.

mathematical_checks.area: Backward radial integration and harmonic extension
mathematical_checks.details: For d>=3 the derivative of t^(d-2)F(tu) has the positive coefficient (d-2)omega_d/(2 drift) times t^(d-3)U_E(tu). Integrating the lower bound U_E>=-C log n backward from 2(b+w) gives the claimed upper bound on F. Local integrability of the kernel and its first derivative justifies differentiation of the bounded compactly supported density; continuity and harmonicity off the support give the interior and exterior extensions. In d=2 F is constant and the mass bound suffices.

The shared positive-potential bound gives the planar global error with logarithmic exponent 3/2. The dimension-specific global martingale bound remains explicit, so the interior proposition retains sqrt(r_n) log n in the plane and sqrt(r_n log n) in higher dimensions. No dropped delta notation or missing auxiliary envelope is needed downstream.

The moment and fixed-site normalizations, bracket constants, finite-dimensional covariance, radial comparisons, separated dipole identities, and lower-tail stopping arguments remain compatible with the assembled potential estimates. The final bulk-deviation sign now agrees with S=-M/sigma in d>=3 and with the stated dipole orientation in d=2.
